reading: Two solid rectangles face each other across a background gap; the gap band between their overlapping extent is filled with 8, trimmed by one cell at each side of the overlap.

new_rows.name: inner_between
new_rows.datalog:
bgc(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), !cell(Y, X, C).
hb(Y, X) :- bgc(Y, X), cell(Y, X1, C1), X1 < X, cell(Y, X2, C2), X2 > X.
vb(Y, X) :- bgc(Y, X), cell(Y1, X, C1), Y1 < Y, cell(Y2, X, C2), Y2 > Y.
inner_between(Y, X) :- hb(Y, X), Ya = Y - 1, hb(Ya, X), Yb = Y + 1, hb(Yb, X).
inner_between(Y, X) :- vb(Y, X), Xa = X - 1, vb(Y, Xa), Xb = X + 1, vb(Y, Xb).

why: every 'between' cell whose two neighbours across the band direction are also between cells becomes 8; plain 'between' would overfill the two edge lines of the overlap

reading: Diamond-outline shapes (and V-shaped parts of diamonds) change size by colour: colour-5 diamonds grow by one ring (radius+1, same centre), colour-2 diamonds shrink by one ring (radius-1; radius 1 becomes a single cell), other colours stay.

slots.subject: each diamond outline object (Manhattan-radius ring about a centre, possibly clipped by the border)

why: on every pair each 5-ring has radius+1 and each 2-ring radius-1 about the same centre; one border-clipped 5 fragment in pair 0 does not fit this exactly

reading: Each closed loop of colour 1 gets a colour-2 ring on the outside cells touching it (8-neighbourhood) and a colour-3 ring on the inside cells touching it; loops with a gap are left alone.

new_rows.name: outer_ring
new_rows.datalog:
bgc(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), !cell(Y, X, C).
off4(DY, DX) :- off(DY, DX), DY = 0.
off4(DY, DX) :- off(DY, DX), DX = 0.
maxy(max(Y)) :- px(Y, X, C).
maxx(max(X)) :- px(Y, X, C).
out(Y, X) :- bgc(Y, X), Y = 0.
out(Y, X) :- bgc(Y, X), X = 0.
out(Y, X) :- bgc(Y, X), maxy(M), Y = M.
out(Y, X) :- bgc(Y, X), maxx(M), X = M.
out(Y2, X2) :- out(Y, X), off4(DY, DX), Y2 = Y + DY, X2 = X + DX, bgc(Y2, X2).
inside(Y, X) :- bgc(Y, X), !out(Y, X).
closed(O) :- inside(Y, X), off(DY, DX), Y2 = Y + DY, X2 = X + DX, obj(O, Y2, X2).
outer_ring(Y, X) :- out(Y, X), off(DY, DX), Y2 = Y + DY, X2 = X + DX, obj(O, Y2, X2), closed(O).

new_rows.name: inner_ring
new_rows.datalog:
bgc(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), !cell(Y, X, C).
off4(DY, DX) :- off(DY, DX), DY = 0.
off4(DY, DX) :- off(DY, DX), DX = 0.
maxy(max(Y)) :- px(Y, X, C).
maxx(max(X)) :- px(Y, X, C).
out(Y, X) :- bgc(Y, X), Y = 0.
out(Y, X) :- bgc(Y, X), X = 0.
out(Y, X) :- bgc(Y, X), maxy(M), Y = M.
out(Y, X) :- bgc(Y, X), maxx(M), X = M.
out(Y2, X2) :- out(Y, X), off4(DY, DX), Y2 = Y + DY, X2 = X + DX, bgc(Y2, X2).
inside(Y, X) :- bgc(Y, X), !out(Y, X).
inner_ring(Y, X) :- inside(Y, X), off(DY, DX), Y2 = Y + DY, X2 = X + DX, cell(Y2, X2, C).

why: first pass: border-reachable (4-connected) background cells 8-adjacent to an object that encloses background become 2; second pass: enclosed background cells 8-adjacent to any non-background cell become 3. Reproduces pairs 0,1,3 exactly; pair 2 has one extra 2 at (13,3) that no adjacency rule explains
invariants: enclosed cells not touching the loop stay background

reading: The grid is a lattice of 3x3 glyphs; every 1-glyph with the same shape as the 8-glyph becomes 8, then every other glyph lying between two 8-glyphs in the same glyph row or glyph column becomes 7.

slots.cells: 3x3 glyphs on a 4-step lattice (blank separator rows/columns)
slots.match_colour: 8 for glyphs identical in shape to the exemplar
slots.between_colour: 7 for non-empty glyphs strictly between two 8-glyphs in one glyph row or column

why: verified on all three pairs: shape matches become 8, row/column betweens of 8-glyphs become 7, everything else stays 1

reading: Two small blocks of different colours sit at opposite ends of the grid; each colour floods its half of the gap toward the other, over the block's width plus one cell on each side, leaving a single background line in the middle when the gap is odd.

slots.subjects: the two coloured blocks, aligned on one axis
slots.extent: floor(gap/2) cells from each block toward the other
slots.breadth: block's cross-extent widened by 1 on each side (the block itself is not widened)
slots.middle: the centre line stays background if the gap length is odd

why: on all pairs each half of the gap takes the colour of the block it touches, one cell wider on each side than the block
invariants: the original blocks keep their cells

reading: The shape is split by one empty row or column inside its bounding box; that line is drawn in 3 across the whole grid.

new_rows.name: gap_line
new_rows.datalog:
miny(min(Y)) :- cell(Y, X, C).
maxy(max(Y)) :- cell(Y, X, C).
minx(min(X)) :- cell(Y, X, C).
maxx(max(X)) :- cell(Y, X, C).
rowhas(Y) :- cell(Y, X, C).
colhas(X) :- cell(Y, X, C).
gap_line(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), miny(A), maxy(B), Y > A, Y < B, !rowhas(Y).
gap_line(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), minx(A), maxx(B), X > A, X < B, !colhas(X).

why: the full grid row or column that is empty and lies strictly inside the foreground's box becomes 3; nothing else changes

reading: On a checkered lattice, a dotted rectangular frame becomes a solid frame with a cleared interior, and the dotted coloured pieces outside it are made solid, packed inside the frame along its long axis (in input order, one-cell gaps, centred) and erased from outside.

slots.container: the dotted rectangle outline (lattice dots of one colour)
slots.pieces: dotted coloured patches outside the frame, each filled solid over its bounding box
slots.arrangement: row or column along the frame's longer interior axis, ordered by input position, separated by one background cell, centred with margin
slots.rest: frame becomes solid lines; interior lattice cleared to background; pieces removed from outside

why: on all three pairs the pieces exactly fit the frame interior with one-cell margins and gaps

reading: A 1-coloured drop at the top falls down its column; if it lands in a watertight cup of colour 2 the cup's interior fills with 1, otherwise (outside or leaky cup) the whole bottom row becomes 1. The drop is removed.

slots.source: the single 1 cell in the top row
slots.container: the 2-walled U shape whose interior contains the drop's column
slots.fill_if_sealed: all background cells inside that cup (between its walls, above its floor) become 1

why: pairs 0,3,4 drop into sealed cups and fill them; pairs 1,2 miss or hit a cup with a hole in its floor and the bottom row fills

reading: Each 9 square of side 2k gets a colour-3 border of thickness k around it, and a colour-1 shadow of the square's width falls from below the border to the bottom of the grid; 3 borders cover 1 shadows, 9 stays on top.

slots.subject: each 9 square
slots.border: 3 ring of thickness half the square's side
slots.shadow: 1 columns under the square (same columns), from below its border to the grid bottom

why: on all four pairs border thickness is side/2 and the shadows run down the square's columns, hidden where a 3 border lies

reading: Every two 1 cells on the same row or column are joined by a line of 8 through the background between them.
why: every background cell between two 1 cells on one row or column becomes 8; nothing else changes
